title: WebUI randomly refreshes without being prompted to
body:
### What happened?

(**Edit 1**: apologies for the unfinished report; I accidentally hit enter while typing.)

This issue first occured around 1-2 months ago and is now affecting 3 out of my 4 devices (the 4th, unaffected device is an Android phone, running v1.27.6).

When interacting with Syncthing though the web UI, the page will just randomly reload - even when there are menus/dialogs open. This is very frustrating, as it will discard any uncommitted changes that I was working on, such as complex ignore patterns or file versioning rules.

As far as logs go, all 3 affected devices only list the mobile device's connection timing out. I attempted turning it off altogether (thus getting rid of the log messages), and while the log messages have cleared up, the issue still persists. There does not seem to be anything in the logs that correlates to the page reloading, in terms of timestamps. The issue seems to occur periodically, sometimes up to 3 times in a minute.

**Edit 2**: Another user reported experiencing this issue [over on Reddit](https://<redacted-host>/r/Syncthing/comments/1bkdstm/webui_constantly_refreshing/). Unfortunately it doesn't seem like it's been resolved. 

### Syncthing version

v1.27.3

### Platform & operating system

Arch Linux (x86-64) / OpenWRT (ARM-64)

### Browser version

Firefox 126

### Relevant log output

_No response_

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: Anything logged in the browser console or happening request wise?

For comparison, a normal (manual) page refresh looks like this:

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
On my third affected device (my OpenWRT router), since I not accessing the web UI through the machine itself, but rather over the network via my Linux system, the behaviour is different. Instead of reloading, the page shows a connection error (as if the daemon was shut down). The browser console then looks like this:

![image](https://github.com/syncthing/syncthing/assets/3143797/32b4e742-e095-47be-ba1d-9f9d2e2b8548)

The daemon however is not actually down, as I am able to manually reload the page to get the WebUI to work again. Not as bad as outright discarding any pending changes, but still annoying.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: I'd try a different browser or disable some plugins

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: I just tested on a clean installation of ungoogled chromium. The issue still occurs on the local machine's WebUI, but doesn't seem to appear on the remote WebUI.

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
I don't think we do anything special depending on whether it's viewed locally or from a remote machine, so that still sounds like something specific to that machine.

Try running syncthing on the other machine and see if you can reproduce that locally.

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
It's noteworthy that the event XHR request fails because of 403 Forbidden,

which causes the page to reload https://github.com/syncthing/syncthing/blob/main/gui/default/syncthing/core/eventService.js#L44

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
I initially thought it was, because uMatrix had disabled cookies for the WebUI. However the issue still happens:
- with cookies enabled on uMatrix
- with uMatrix turned off
- with the uMatrix addon completely disabled
- with the fresh install of ungoogled Chromium (which has no addons)

I might've missed a test case, but I suspect it's probably not cookie related.

Another finding from looking at the network graph of the remote WebUI is that the endpoint request eventually fails with "CSRF Error", triggering a page reload (likely via the file @participant4 posted).

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: This might be related to #7399. Maybe Chromium is a bit more strict?

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Huh. In that case, maybe the CSRF Cookie expires after a while, which causes the backend to return 403 when Syncthing attempts to do a periodic update, and that in turn causes the page to reload.

In which case: is this an intended feature? And can it be turned off?

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: "csrf error" typically just means auth error, doesn't need to be the csrf specifically. I suspect something yeeting the auth cookie.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
We're not setting the `SameSite` attribute for the `CSRF-TOKEN-XXXXXXX` and `sessionid-XXXXXX` cookies. Maybe Ungoogled Chromium is a bit more strict in that regard?

Not sure if this intended or not, but the CSRF cookie is also missing the `Secure` attribute.

![grafik](https://github.com/syncthing/syncthing/assets/1926175/61e2cdad-0404-498b-acca-df6cedd6152b)

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Update on my situation:

about a month ago I decided to change the GUI listen address across my desktop and laptop. Additionally I went ahead and cleared my page cookies after I had everything set up, to make sure I was starting out in a relatively fresh state. So far the issue hasn't come up again, but I don't know what ultimately fixed it...

If it really was cookies, then that wouldn't explain why the issue appeared on a completely fresh browser with a brand new user profile. But then again, I don't know what else to pin it on. In any case, glad it's resolved for now.

On an unrelated note, thank you all for working on this project. I didn't think to say it last time, and I worry it didn't come across due to the nature of the conversation, but I genuinely appreciate having Syncthing in my life (especially as a dev).

comments.author: participant5
comments.body:
I have the same problem here, only with a headless Raspberry Pi OS ARM32 with version v1.27.12 (this refreshing is happening for months).
I've tried a few browsers in 2 computers. I also noticed some 403 HTTP errors in console just before refreshing page, and a lot of "CSRF-TOKEN-XXXXXXX" cookie (with the same name). On other servers, there is only one CSRF-TOKEN-XXXXXXX and one sessionid-XXXXXX.
